title: Introduction to Free-Floating Subdivisions
summary: Explains how to read the LCSH list of free-floating subdivisions (SUBDIVISIONS.pdf), generated from LC subdivision authority records (created since 1999) and current as of April 2026. Authorized subdivisions are in boldface after a long dash; multi-subfield subdivisions are shown with successive dashes; (May Subd Geog) marks those that may be further subdivided geographically; each entry carries the controlling SHM sheet code(s) (H 1095-H 1200), a usage note giving its category (topical, form, chronological) and the heading types it may be used under, and sometimes a restriction note. USE/UF (with [Former subdivision]) and BT/NT references link subdivision terms. The only geographic subdivision on the list is --Foreign countries.
validation_rules: The free-floating subdivisions list is the full set of subdivisions authorized for free-floating use in LCSH as of April 2026, generated from subdivision authority records in the LCSH Master Database; LC began creating subdivision authority records to control free-floating topical, form, and chronological subdivisions in 1999. A subdivision not on the list (and not authorized by a pattern heading or printed under a specific heading) is not free-floating. (FF Intro para. 1)

The list contains exactly one geographic subdivision: `--Foreign countries`. All other entries are topical, form, or chronological subdivisions. Geographic names (other than `--Foreign countries`) are not free-floating subdivisions from this list; they are added only after elements marked (May Subd Geog). (FF Intro para. 1)

Authorized subdivisions appear in boldface following a long dash, e.g., `—Anatomy`; `—Civilization`. The long dash (—) in the printed list corresponds to the subdivision delimiter `--` in a heading string (MARC `$x`/`$v`/`$y`/`$z`). An entry not in boldface (e.g., a USE reference lead-in) is not an authorized subdivision. (FF Intro para. 2)

Some subdivisions consist of more than one subfield, e.g., `—Antiquities—Collection and preservation`. Such a multi-subfield subdivision is authorized as a unit: its parts must appear together, in the printed order, as consecutive subdivisions (`--Antiquities--Collection and preservation`). (FF Intro para. 2)

The legend `(May Subd Geog)` following a subdivision means it is authorized for further geographic subdivision, e.g., `—Commerce (May Subd Geog)`; a geographic subdivision may then follow that subdivision. A subdivision without the legend may not be followed directly by a geographic subdivision (see LCSH Introduction, Geographic Subdivisions). (FF Intro para. 2)

Indented under each subdivision on the next line are the code(s) identifying the controlling Subject Headings Manual instruction sheet number(s) for that subdivision (H 1095–H 1200). Consult the controlling sheet(s) for the categories of headings under which the subdivision is free-floating. [Cross-reference, not stated in this introduction: H 1095 general; H 1100 classes of persons; H 1103 ethnic groups; H 1105 corporate bodies; H 1110 persons; H 1120 families; H 1140 places; H 1145.5 bodies of water; H 1147–H 1200 pattern headings.] (FF Intro para. 2)

Each entry carries a usage note identifying the category of the subdivision (topical, form, or chronological) and the types of headings under which its use is authorized. Use a subdivision only under the heading types its usage note authorizes, and only in the function (topical `$x`, form `$v`, chronological `$y`) that the note states. (FF Intro para. 3)

Many form subdivisions also function as topical subdivisions and have dual entries; the same term may therefore be valid as `$v` (form: what the work is) or as `$x` (topical: what the work is about), but each function is governed by its own entry and usage note. (FF Intro para. 3)

Some entries have an additional note with further information or restrictions, e.g., "Further subdivide by subdivisions used under classes of persons;" "Do not subdivide geographically under names of individual persons." Such notes restrict use of the subdivision (including its geographic subdivision) for the heading types they name and must be applied in addition to the usage note. (FF Intro para. 3)

USE references lead from an unauthorized or non-preferred subdivision term to the authorized or preferred subdivision, e.g., `—Anniversary celebrations USE —Anniversaries, etc.`; `—Assimilation, Cultural USE —Cultural assimilation`. A string containing the non-preferred term (e.g., `--Anniversary celebrations`, `--Assimilation, Cultural`) is invalid; replace it with the USE target. (FF Intro para. 4)

Under authorized subdivisions, the tracings of USE references appear after the code `UF` (Used For). A UF term labeled `[Former subdivision]` is an earlier form of the subdivision and must not be used in new strings. (FF Intro para. 4)

Authorized subdivisions are linked hierarchically by reciprocal `BT` (broader term subdivision) and `NT` (narrower term subdivision) references; these express hierarchy, not permissible ordering in a string. (FF Intro para. 4)

New subdivisions are added and existing ones revised at LC editorial meetings; changes are announced in the Summary of Decisions accompanying the L.C. Subject Headings Monthly Lists, and new/revised subdivision authority records are distributed weekly via the MARC Distribution Service—Subject Authorities. A subdivision's validity can therefore change after April 2026. (FF Intro para. 1)

sections.heading: Introduction to Free-Floating Subdivisions
sections.text:
This is a list of subdivisions that are authorized for free-floating use in the Library of Congress Subject Heading system. This current list was generated from data gleaned from subdivision authority records that are online in the LCSH Master Database at the Library of Congress. The Library of Congress began to create subdivision authority records to control free-floating topical, form, and chronological subdivisions in 1999. The list represents the full set of free-floating subdivisions in existence as of April 2026 and includes one geographic subdivision, —Foreign countries. New subdivisions are added and existing subdivisions are revised at editorial meetings at the Library of Congress. Announcements of new and revised free-floating subdivisions are made in the Summary of Decisions accompanying the L.C. Subject Headings Monthly Lists that are posted to the World Wide Web at https://www.loc.gov/aba/cataloging/subject/weeklylists/. New and revised subdivision authority records are distributed to subscribers in the weekly MARC Distribution Service—Subject Authorities. More information on free-floating subdivisions and their use may be found in the Subject Headings Manual. Questions on free-floating subdivisions may be sent to the Policy, Training, and Cooperative Programs Division at policy@loc.gov.

Authorized subdivisions appear in boldface type following a long dash, e.g., **—Anatomy**; **—Civilization**. Some subdivisions consist of more than one subfield, e.g., **—Antiquities—Collection and preservation**. For those subdivisions that are authorized for further geographic subdivision, the legend (May Subd Geog) appears following the subdivision, e.g., **—Commerce** (May Subd Geog). Indented under the subdivision in the next line are the code(s) that identify the controlling instruction sheet number(s) for the subdivision in the Subject Headings Manual (H 1095-H 1200).

A usage note that identifies the category of the subdivision (topical, form, or chronological) and the types of headings with which its use is authorized appears with each subdivision entry. Dual entries have been made for the many form subdivisions that can also function as topical subdivisions. For some subdivisions, there is an additional note with further information or restrictions on use of the subdivision, e.g., "Further subdivide by subdivisions used under classes of persons;" "Do not subdivide geographically under names of individual persons."

Cross-references similar to those made to subject headings appear with subdivision entries in this list. USE references are made from an unauthorized or non-preferred subdivision term to an authorized or preferred subdivision, e.g., —Anniversary celebrations USE —Anniversaries, etc.; —Assimilation, Cultural USE —Cultural assimilation. Under authorized subdivisions, tracings of those references appear following the code UF (Used For). UF references that represent earlier forms of a subdivision are identified by the legend [Former subdivision]. Authorized subdivisions are linked to each other hierarchically by reciprocal BT/NT references. BT references represent broader term subdivisions while NT references represent narrower term subdivisions.
